problem: Existing hierarchical 3D scene graphs assume a static world and treat all blocking objects (boxes, screens, trolleys, doors) as permanent obstacles, causing detours or unreachable targets. Their room and object semantics are also noisy: cross-room contamination in room features and fragmented 2D-projected object nodes.
motivation: Humans judge whether a blocking object can be moved and push it aside to take shorter routes or reach otherwise blocked areas. Encoding movability inside the navigation graph would give scene-graph-based planners higher reachability and efficiency, but this needs cleaner room and object semantics first.
key_idea: Build a hierarchical traversable 3D scene graph that inserts movable obstacles into the Voronoi navigation graph as interactive nodes, selected by an efficiency score (K-shell iteration factor) plus VLM semantic filtering.
insight: Movability should be judged by whether interaction improves global graph efficiency, not by physical properties alone. Efficiency filtering cuts VLM calls from 121 to 34 and raises recognition accuracy (33.33/41.67 vs 10.81/17.24 for SF-only). Removing the structural (Seg.) module of the topological clustering drops grounding Acc@0.25 from 59.8 to 10.1, and CLIP beats SigLIP in the full pipeline (59.8 vs 56.5), so encoder–pipeline compatibility matters. Visibility Purification raises room-retrieval success from 14/20 to 20/20.
method: Coarse-grained graph: floor split by height-histogram peaks + DBSCAN; rooms by BEV occupancy, distance transform, Otsu seeds and watershed
Visibility Purification Strategy: per-view visibility weight (share of room BEV grid covered) used in weighted K-means over CLIP embeddings to get room-consistent features

Topological Clustering Strategy: superpoints (VCCS + region growing, GrowSP-style), a superpoint graph with SAM-mask-based, visibility-weighted affinities, progressive merging (threshold relaxed 0.9→0.5 over 5 stages) into object nodes, then semantic refinement by local SAM-prompt recovery and multi-scale global context
Voronoi navigation graph: BEV navigable area from camera poses + floor support − obstacles, Voronoi skeleton sampled into waypoints
Efficiency Filtering: insert a candidate object into the nav graph and rank it by KS^IF (K-shell coreness and iteration depth); below threshold δ it counts as immovable
Semantic Filtering: Gemini-2.5-Pro (temperature 0) takes an object crop plus scene view and returns a binary movable label
Topological Update: confirmed movable obstacles become interactive nodes linked by distance-adaptive, visibility-checked edges

setting.backbone: CLIP ViT-H-14 (frozen) for semantics; SAM/Semantic-SAM for masks; Gemini-2.5-Pro (frozen) for movability filtering; GPT-5 only in a grounding ablation
setting.observation: RGB-D + camera poses (1080x720, 90° HFOV, 1.5 m height), panoramic scanning for graph building
setting.action_space: waypoint traversal on a Voronoi topological graph; interaction with movable obstacles is abstracted (movable nodes are passable)
setting.simulator: Habitat-Sim (HM3D scenes augmented with movable obstacles)
setting.privileged: RGB-D and poses collected by pre-exploration of the scene to build the graph; obstacles manually placed; no other GT stated

numbers.eval_set_note: Scene 1 (not blocking, 4 movable, 20 tasks); custom augmented HM3D benchmark
numbers.extra: pre-built scene graph from scanning; baseline is modified HOV-SG (baseline: PL 19.0, SR 80.0)

numbers_note: Navigation Table 4 has 8 per-scene rows on a custom benchmark; only three representative rows are listed. Other rows are in the paper (e.g., ID 2: SR 100.0, SPL 73.9).
results: On the custom augmented HM3D benchmark HERO reduces path length by about 35% in partially obstructed scenes and raises SR in fully blocked scenes (e.g., 5% to 85% in scene 4) against a non-interactive HOV-SG-based baseline. It also beats HOV-SG on ScanNetV2 (mAcc 56.4 vs 43.1) and on ScanRefer grounding (Acc@0.25 58.3 vs 16.4) using CLIP only.
limitations: Evaluation uses a self-built small benchmark (8 scenes, 160 tasks, 18 hand-placed obstacles of 4 categories) against a single modified baseline
Interaction is abstracted; no physical manipulation is executed and there are no real-robot experiments
Requires pre-exploration to build the graph and relies on a proprietary VLM for movability with a low recognition accuracy (max 41.67%)
